drops.line: The field set. Sent out sharp and clean, both at once.
drops.why: Matthew 10 is marching orders: go, travel light, be shrewd without losing your innocence. Washed black, washed blue, black — three colorways of one field set, because the mission is real and it is one mission.

briefing.mission: Marching orders: go light, go wise, go anyway.

points.p: The twelve get named before they get sent. Identity precedes assignment: you're a person on the roster, not a number in a crowd.
No gold, no bag, no second coat. The mission funds the mission, and everything you'd over-pack is weight the road doesn't need.
The line on the back of the set: shrewd and clean at the same time. Neither cancels the other: wisdom without edge, innocence without naivety.
Fear gets answered with worth: not one sparrow falls unnoticed, and you are counted down to the hair. Courage here is arithmetic, not bravado.

questions: What would 'travel light' have you put down this season?
Where do you need more serpent, and where more dove?
What's the assignment you keep waiting to feel ready for?
briefing.prayer: Lord, send me sharp and keep me clean. Give me wisdom that doesn't harden and innocence that doesn't fold. I'll go. Amen.

benched.line: The closer. The season ends where the book does: with a sending.
benched.why: Matthew 28 is the Great Commission: all authority, then go. The lightest colorway closes the season the way the resurrection closes the Gospel: walking out in daylight.

briefing.mission: The tomb is open and the credential is signed. Go make disciples.

points.p: The women get the news first and running becomes the right response. The season's lightest colorway starts at a grave that didn't hold.
The commission opens with the credential, not the command. 'All authority in heaven and on earth' is the backing on every assignment that follows.
The assignment is reproduction: disciples who make disciples. Not an audience. A lineage.
The book closes on presence, not pressure: 'I am with you always, even to the end of the age.' The walk is accompanied.

questions: If the authority is His, what exactly are you still waiting to be qualified for?
Who taught you, and who are you teaching?
Where does 'with you always' need to land in your week?
briefing.prayer: Jesus, You hold the authority and I hold the assignment. Walk with me all the days. I'll walk in purpose. Amen.

emblems.name: The M
emblems.meaning: The house mark. Steel and ruby, cut as a chevron: the name everything else on the garment is made under.

scripture.text: He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies. To him who overcomes, to him I will give of the hidden manna, and I will give him a white stone, and on the stone a new name written, which no one knows but he who receives it.

emblems.note: The mark is white stone with the name cut into it. That is the verse, literally.

emblems.name: Heav' Yeah
emblems.meaning: The front crest, and the whole point of the drop. It replaces the idiom 'hell yeah', because the answer is never yes to hell. The yes only ever goes one direction.

scripture.text: For however many are the promises of God, in him is the “Yes.” Therefore also through him is the “Amen”, to the glory of God through us.
But let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes’ and your ‘No’ be ‘No.’ Whatever is more than these is of the evil one.

emblems.note: Two verses because it is two claims: Christ is the Yes (2 Cor 1:20), and what you say yes to is not a small thing (Mt 5:37). Changing an idiom is a speech act, and Matthew 5 is the speech verse.

emblems.name: Seek First the Kingdom
emblems.meaning: The left sleeve. The order of operations for a whole life, stacked vertically so you read it top to bottom like a command.

scripture.text: But seek first God’s Kingdom, and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.

emblems.note: Printed on the garment with the reference already on it.

emblems.name: The Overwatch
emblems.meaning: The drone at the top of the sleeve lockup. Not a weapon here — an eye. Something above you that does not blink, and is on your side.

scripture.text: For Yahweh’s eyes run back and forth throughout the whole earth, to show himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him.

emblems.note: Cut from the head of the Seek First lockup. Showing the whole lockup for all three of its marks said nothing; each one carries the part it is.

emblems.name: The Morning Star
emblems.meaning: The interlaced six-point star in its compass, at the foot of the sleeve. A figure that is drawn from one unbroken band and keeps returning through itself.

scripture.text: I, Jesus, have sent my angel to testify these things to you for the assemblies. I am the root and the offspring of David; the Bright and Morning Star.

emblems.note: Root and offspring at once — the same line arriving from both ends, which is what the interlace draws. If the intent behind it was replication rather than the star of David, 2 Timothy 2:2 is the verse instead: what you were taught, commit to faithful people who will teach others also.

emblems.name: War and Peace
emblems.meaning: The twin slash on both sleeves. Two bars, two seasons: wartime and peacetime. You do not get to pick which one you are in, only how you carry it.

scripture.text: a time to love, and a time to hate; a time for war, and a time for peace.

emblems.note: Two lines for the two times. The verse is one sentence with the same shape.

emblems.meaning: The number in the crown of thorns. The age He was when it finished — and the chapter and verse of the sleeve, Matthew 6:33. The drop's own arithmetic: the number is the age and the address at the same time.

scripture.text: When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, “It is finished.” He bowed his head, and gave up his spirit.
They braided a crown of thorns and put it on his head, and a reed in his right hand; and they kneeled down before him, and mocked him, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!”

emblems.note: The wreath is the crown of thorns (Mt 27:29); the number is what it cost (Jn 19:30).

emblems.name: The Hitman Halo
emblems.meaning: The HM with the round through it, under the halo. The name is a provocation on purpose: a hitman takes a contract and does not miss. The halo says whose contract, and the scripture says what the target is — and is not.

scripture.text: For our wrestling is not against flesh and blood, but against the principalities, against the powers, against the world’s rulers of the darkness of this age, and against the spiritual forces of wickedness in the heavenly places.
for the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh, but mighty before God to the throwing down of strongholds,

emblems.note: ART PENDING: the new HM mark is on its way and replaces assets/img/hm-mark.png here. Ephesians 6:12 is load-bearing for this mark — it is the verse that says the target is never a person, which is the only thing that makes the name wearable.

emblemsNote: EVERY MARK ON THE GARMENT MEANS SOMETHING, and the meaning is carried here rather than in anyone's memory. Scripture is World English Bible, public domain, the same translation the chapter rooms serve. Quote it exactly or not at all.
